key_insight: Disordered metal-oxide photonic glasses can produce building-integrated PV colors without strong iridescence, but the achievable color depends more on oxide choice and stack design than on disorder alone.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a practical design map for tunable, low-loss colored PV facades, helping engineers balance aesthetics, spectral selectivity, and power yield.
method: Modeled color formation using Mie scattering, Percus–Yevick structure factors, exact phase functions, and two-flux transfer.
Explored four target facade colors across four oxides, four encapsulants, two cell technologies, and wide ranges of particle size, packing fraction, and layer count.
Evaluated color shift under realistic viewing and sun-angle changes on a laminated three-layer coating stack.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that all four target colors were reached within DeltaE00 0.8 to 2.5 in a laminated three-layer coating, while angular variation caused DeltaE00 shifts of 5 to 18 over the day.
watch_item: Angle independence is limited in realistic use: facade geometry and sun/view angles can noticeably shift perceived color, so the coating must be co-designed with installation conditions.
paper_title: Engineering Color and Angular Stability in Building-Integrated Photovoltaics Using Metal-Oxide Photonic Glasses
